script.title: The Navy Wanted the Golden Gate Bridge in Stripes
sentences: The Navy wanted the Golden Gate Bridge striped black and yellow.
It opened in 1937, across a strait many experts said could not be bridged.
Passing ships had to see the thing.
The Navy also feared a ship collision could block the entrance to one of its main harbors.
Chief engineer Joseph Strauss didn't pick the color.
Irving Morrow did, a relatively unknown residential architect, and he chose International Orange.
So a house architect beat the US Navy, on what Frommer's calls the most photographed bridge in the world.
script.description:
The US Navy wanted black and yellow stripes on the Golden Gate Bridge.
An unknown house architect picked International Orange instead.
visuals: Golden Gate Bridge International Orange tower
Golden Gate Bridge from Marin Headlands
claims_en: The US Navy suggested the Golden Gate Bridge be painted with black and yellow stripes.
Many experts said a bridge could not be built across the strait.
The stripes were meant to ensure visibility by passing ships.
The US Navy feared a ship collision could block the entrance to one of its main harbors.
Joseph Strauss was the chief engineer.
The International Orange color was the personal selection of Irving Morrow.
Irving Morrow was a relatively unknown residential architect.
Morrow's choice won out over the Navy's suggestion.
Frommer's travel guide describes it as certainly the most photographed bridge in the world.
